metadata.title: Matrix Maps Basis and Shape
metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.objective: Show how a matrix maps basis vectors and a shape in the plane.
metadata.learner: Has seen vectors but not matrix geometry.
misconceptions: Matrix multiplication is just elementwise multiplication
expectedUnderstanding: The matrix columns are the images of the basis vectors
Every vertex of the shape transforms by the same rule
The determinant a gives the area scale for this matrix

checkpoints.title: Columns are basis images
checkpoints.body: Set a to 1.4 and b to 0.6. The transformed e1 arrow ends at the first column (1.4, 0); the transformed e2 arrow ends at the second column (0.6, 1).
checkpoints.learnerAction: Set a to 1.4 and b to 0.6.

checkpoints.title: Shear moves e2
checkpoints.body: Set b to 0. The shear vanishes and the transformed shape becomes a rectangle, but its area scale is still a.

checkpoints.title: Area scales by a
checkpoints.body: Set a to 2 and b to 0. The square is twice as wide, and det = 2, so its area doubles. Every corner still comes from the same matrix rule.
checkpoints.learnerAction: Set a to 2 and b to 0.

narration.text: The faint unit square and basis arrows show the original grid; the moving arrows are the matrix columns.
Changing b shears the second basis vector sideways, and every transformed corner follows.
Changing a stretches the first basis vector; the determinant tracks the area scale.

fallback.text: The unit square and basis arrows are transformed by the matrix with columns (a, 0) and (b, 1). The transformed basis arrows end at those columns, and every corner follows the same map; determinant a gives the area scale.

accessibility.alt: A unit square and two basis arrows at the origin, plus their transformed images under a shear-and-scale matrix. Sliders change entries a and b; transformed corners and basis arrows move together.
